messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx and connection resets from inference endpoints in us-west-2a (obs: 5xx spike @ 3162501200). Linking dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/alerts/3162501234 :pager:

maya: oncall here, acknowledging. pulling metrics now. seeing 5xx -> 50% on /v1/generate for model-redwood-small in us-west-2a. Latency also up on routing tier.

maya: quick triage - curl to edge from our probe:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer x"
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.example (54.x.x.x) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< Connection: close
```

rachel: logs from runtime shard usw2a-rt-03 show repeated tls connection resets and socket recv errors: `recv: Connection reset by peer` around 3162501100-3162501220.

network-eng: we see increased UDP RX drops on the resolver instances in us-west-2a on the host NICs. counters jumped ~3k/5m on a subset of AZ hosts. This correlates with resolver timeouts in our vpc-dns cache.

eng-runtime: that matches KV cache misses - clients fall back to origin and we hit instance connection churn. Recommend steering traffic off us-west-2a to standby AZ for now. Can we apply a routing policy change?

maya: agree. applying temporary smart-router policy to prefer us-west-2b for model-redwood-small canaries. command:
```
redwoodctl routing update --model model-redwood-small --from-zone us-west-2a --to-zone us-west-2b --weight 90
```

maya: executed. new policy pushed at 3162501400. watching.

network-eng: opened AWS support case 1234567891 for suspected host-level NIC RX drops; noted with AWS NLB team. aws-support-bot: Case created: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/1234567891

maya: after steering, 5xx dropped from 50% -> 8% in ~90s. latency increased ~40ms for the affected flows (expected due to cross-AZ).

customer-success-bot: flagging impacted customers: tenant-alpha and tenant-gamma reported errors. CS is drafting messages and will coordinate.

liam: what's long-term plan? if AWS reports noisy NICs we may need to evacuate instance fleet in us-west-2a or scale dedicated capacity in another AZ. Also need post-incident actions for resolver caching hardening.

rachel: runtime notes - we saw many TLS sessions stalls and re-establish attempts; KCACHE metrics show >10% prefix cache evictions under this pattern. Putting a conservative kvcache TTL bump might reduce origin fallback while we move traffic.

eng-runtime: applying kvcache TTL change now:
```
redwoodctl config set kvcache.ttl --model model-redwood-small --value 15s
```

eng-runtime: TTL bump applied at 3162501560. monitoring for hit-rate improvements.

maya: also rotated NLB target health-check window to be more tolerant for a short window:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --health-check-interval-seconds 10 --healthy-threshold-count 3
```

network-eng: AWS team replied: they see RX drops at the hypervisor level correlated with host NIC driver bug on a small subset of instances in us-west-2a. They are recommending instance replacement and host-patching. ETA for first remediation wave ~2 hours.

maya: immediate mitigations are working. 5xx stabilized under 5% after routing change + TTL bump. continuing to monitor for client errors and SLO impact.

customer-success-bot: tenant-alpha support ticket updated. we sent temporary mitigation notice and ETA for full remediation.

liam: prepping for handoff in 30m. if AWS remediation takes >1.5h we'll schedule instance evacuation and capacity increase in us-west-2b/d. Can someone create runbook checklist for evacuation?

maya: created checklist gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/evac-runbook-3162501234 (includes drain -> reprovision -> reattach targets -> verify kvcache warm).

network-eng: action item logged: escalate AWS case if more hosts become affected; track host id list; try to avoid noisy-instance placement in future.

aws-support-bot: update: case 1234567891 - remediation started, patching wave scheduled. will update when hosts replaced.

rachel: adding postmortem owner: liam. he will collect timeline, impact metrics, and tracking for resolver/cache hardening.

liam: taking over incident lead. thanks everyone. leaving a short note for next oncall: keep routing steer until AWS confirms all affected hosts are replaced and NLB health returns to normal. :white_check_mark:

maya: handing off to liam at 3162501860. incident state: mitigated (partial) - customer-visible errors reduced; root cause suspected NIC/host driver-level packet drops in us-west-2a. follow-ups: patching progress, kvcache config review, routing fallback playbook.

incident-bot: Incident summary created: https://console.redwood/incidents/3162501234 — status: Mitigated (partial). Pager: maya -> liam. Postmortem owner: liam.
